svg.title: The Orchestrator lifecycle: from request to verified delivery
svg.desc: Nine-stage lifecycle showing how the Lead orchestrator frames work, routes it to producer souls, gates it through an independent verifier, integrates it, and publishes the result.
svg.text: The Orchestrator lifecycle: from request to verified delivery
Nine-stage lifecycle showing how the Lead orchestrator frames work, routes it to producer souls, gates it through an independent verifier, integrates it, and publishes the result.
One request, nine control points, evidence at every handoff.
The Lead follows this sequence, but moves backward whenever evidence changes the plan or a gate fails.

text.tspan: Intake & objective
The human enables Orchestrator mode and states the goal. The Lead records the objective, acceptance criteria,
authorized scope, constraints, budgets, and material decisions. Preliminary inspection is allowed before planning.
Objective record · acceptance criteria · authorized scope · open decisions
Plan & ledger
Decompose around coherent deliverables. Give every item a stable ID, outcome, owner, acceptance, dependencies,
verification, and effort budget. Choose the smallest useful team; reserve effort for integration and review.
Published plan · work-item outline · Team task board entries · remaining
retry allowance
Route & dispatch
Consult the live soul catalog and definitions. Match each item to the smallest capable soul: researcher for evidence,
software engineer for code, scribe for docs, generalist when nothing fits. Resolve fresh versus forked context.
Self-contained assignment · exact soul name · owned resources · checks ·
return format
Execute in soul context
The teammate works inside its own operating contract: inspect before acting, stay inside ownership, run the assigned
checks, perform author review, and prepare an identifiable candidate. It reports facts and limits, not just a success
claim.
Candidate artifact + revision · checks run · author review · soul-defined
handoff
Assess & freeze
Compare the report with acceptance criteria. Distinguish reported completion, review verdict, and Lead acceptance.
Freeze an inspectable candidate and assemble a neutral review packet with its exact identity and known limitations.
Evidence assessment · ledger update · frozen candidate · review packet
Independent review
A separate qualified verifier challenges the candidate against its requirements. It may inspect and probe, but never edits
the deliverable. It returns one candidate-bound verdict and evidence-backed findings with locations and impact.
PASS / REVISE / BLOCKED · findings + coverage gaps · independence limits
Correct & reverify
The Lead dispositions findings, assigns corrections to the producer with the affected evidence, and keeps the remaining
cycle budget visible. The revised candidate returns for a new verdict; prior results cover only the earlier version.
Corrected candidate · finding dispositions · cycles used / remaining · new
verdict

g.text: ↻ repeats until PASS or the cycle budget is exhausted

text.tspan: Integrate & publish
After all workers stop editing, integrate accepted results and run checks on the combined deliverable. The Lead alone
owns Git: inspect the tree, branch, commit only task changes, push, open or update the PR, and read CI.
Integrated result · final commit · PR URL · CI status (or explicit waiver)
Report & close
Close only when acceptance criteria are met, required gates are resolved, and the PR is delivered or waived. Report the
result, evidence, limitations, and authorized exceptions. A failed or unperformed gate is never described as a pass.
Final response · PR / commit / CI summary · disclosed limitations · durable
checkpoint

svg.text: TWO RULES THAT KEEP THE LOOP HONEST

text.tspan: A successful tool return, a finished teammate, or a completed review is not acceptance. Acceptance applies only to the reviewed
candidate and scope.
Direct work by the Lead follows the same gates. Independence cannot be claimed when the verifier authored the candidate; disclose
the conflict or obtain separate coverage.
